All three are plain value types. A ZEROED Parms buffer is therefore a valid construction and needs no InitializeStruct and no destruction -- which is what keeps this gate inside already-proven assignment semantics.
2_required_parameters.every_bool_is_a_full_byte: StackSearch, ShowNotifications, RemainingItem and every bool in the three structs report is_bitfield=false, FieldMask 0xff, ByteOffset 0. No bitfield write is required anywhere.
2_required_parameters.how_ProcessEvent_consumes_Parms: FMemory::Memcpy(Frame, Parms, Function->ParmsSize) copies the caller's buffer in (ScriptCore.cpp:2080-2083), and each out parameter's PropAddr is set to ContainerPtrToValuePtr<uint8>(Parms) (ScriptCore.cpp:2100-2107) -- so out values are written back DIRECTLY into our own buffer and can be read there afterwards.
2_required_parameters.eventgraph_fastcall_hazard: UE_BLUEPRINT_EVENTGRAPH_FASTCALLS is 1 unconditionally, including Shipping (Build.h:365). If UFunction::EventGraphFunction were non-null, ProcessEvent would REPLACE our Parms with a 4-byte int (ScriptCore.cpp:2041-2049). The macro's own comment restricts the optimisation to 'event thunks into an event graph that have no parameters', and AddItem has six -- but the live confirmation (reading UFunction+0xC8 for AddItem against a known event stub such as CreateNotificationInChild as a positive control) was NOT completed before the process exited. 6_registration_target.summary: The definition resolver reads MasterItemList (a UCompositeDataTable), not ItemList. But UDataTable::AddRow on ItemList broadcasts OnDataTableChanged, MasterItemList is the single subscriber to that delegate (verified live by weak-pointer index AND serial), and the handler rebuilds the composite from its parents. So the already-proven primitive on ItemList does reach the resolver, and no new mechanism is needed.
